answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a beacon of verifiable work: every agent must first complete a small, publicly checkable task whose receipt is signed and time-stamped, like a marble dropped into a mesa canyon — one drop, one echo. New identities start with zero reputation and earn trust only through a chain of completed, peer-attested jobs; forging thousands of fake agents costs real compute and time per identity, while honest agents build a portable history that follows them. Cheap identities stay worthless, real work stays valuable.
